items.prompt: Starting with three fourths, we’ve seen how to write an equivalent fraction with twenty on the bottom. 3/4 × 5/5 = 15/20 But what if we went the other way? What if we started with fifteen over twenty, and wanted an equivalent fraction with four on the bottom? Well, we write the equation exactly the same way, with the smaller numbers on the left, and the bigger numbers on the right.
items.demo: *▢/4 × ▢/▢ = 15/20* — the smaller numbers on the left, and the bigger numbers on the right.

items.prompt: So if I want a fraction with five on the bottom, that’s equivalent to fifteen over twenty… ▢/5 15/20 I write this equation to help me.
And if I want an equation with three on top that’s equivalent to fifteen over twenty… 3/▢ 15/20 I write this equation to help me.

Your turn to write the equation that will help find the equivalent fraction. We’re starting with fifteen over twenty, and we want an equivalent fraction with five on the bottom. Write the equation that will help us. ▢/5 15/20
items.demo: The smaller numbers go on the left, and the bigger numbers on the right: ▢/5 × ▢/▢ = *15/20*.
